sources.entry: Nocturne - Makes the menu bar clock unreadable so it stops telling you how late it is, without hiding anything or asking for permissions.

summary.one_liner: Nocturne is a free, MIT-licensed macOS menu bar app that makes the system clock unreadable (analog dial, or covered) so it stops showing the time, and can follow Focus modes.
summary.what_it_does: Switches the macOS menu bar clock to an analog dial (Blind mode, the default) so the time is no longer readable at a glance. Other modes draw a patch over the clock (Gone, experimental, leaves a faint seam), blank the whole menu bar except its own icon (Hide everything), or blank everything except the clock (Only the clock). Hover-to-show temporarily uncovers the bar while the pointer is on it. A Focus filter lets a Focus such as Do Not Disturb switch the mode on when it starts and restore the previous mode when it ends. Settings can individually turn off the day of week, date, or AM/PM in the clock. The README says it needs no permissions and uses no private APIs, and that it restores the IsAnalog clock setting on quit.
use_cases: hide the time in the macOS menu bar
stop seeing the clock during focus work
automatically hide clock when Do Not Disturb is on
blank menu bar icons for distraction-free screen
make the menu bar clock analog or unreadable
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL not given in README>
notable: Makes the clock unreadable rather than hidden, since macOS offers no clock visibility toggle
Follows Focus through a Focus filter with no permissions required
Hover-to-show lets you look at the time on demand
Restores your original Clock Options on quit and documents a manual undo command
README documents measured widths, CPU use and the Focus detection approach in detail
caveats: The Gone mode is labelled experimental and leaves a faint visible seam
Full-screen Spaces are not covered unless the menu bar is set to stay visible
Restoring always returns the clock to digital, even if it was analog before install
